consumer_contexts: games and social experiences on several headset platforms that open world-anchored panels, a wrist menu, and a palm-summoned hand menu, route controller-ray, poke, and gaze input to exactly one panel, and restyle every panel from one skin without forking prefabs

training, industrial, and accessibility XR applications that dock secondary controls to a primary panel, let a panel follow the person with lag, replay a session's panel state deterministically for review, and switch between UGUI and UI Toolkit compositions without changing the shell contract
common_kernel: panel, wrist-menu, and hand-menu identity as validated identities separate from the Canvas, document, transform, or hand pose that implements them

a shell layout model with a closed set of anchor kinds (world, head-locked, wrist, hand) and placement intents (open, close, focus, dock, follow) applied to an immutable state with stable failure codes and deterministic replay
pointer and gaze routing as typed hover, select, and scroll intents from a named input source that resolve to exactly one panel or an explicit ambiguity failure
a skin contract that maps the shared design-language tokens to a closed set of named slots with fail-closed rejection of an unknown token, an unknown slot, or an unmapped slot
sibling UGUI and UI Toolkit adapters that each expose one injectable skin seam and a default skin carrying the canonical values, with evidence that never transfers between them
configurable_variation: which panels, menus, and anchor kinds a product declares, which panel holds exclusive focus, and which input sources it registers
adapter-side binding to world-space Canvas or UIDocument surfaces, event cameras, raycasters, input modules, anchor transforms, and follow parameters
consumer-owned skins injected through the seam, panel content, menu items, prefabs, and scene layout
excluded_project_specific: one product's menu structure, panel content, brand skin, prefab hierarchy, and scene placement values
one project's hand-tracking pose thresholds, input bindings, comfort presets, and platform store review outcome
rationale: A world-space UI shell is a recurring cross-project need whose kernel (validated panel and menu identity, a closed anchor-kind and placement-intent model over immutable state, routing of a named pointer or gaze source to exactly one panel, and a token-to-slot skin contract) is shared by the engine's own world-space Canvas, UI Toolkit, and XR UI integration, by three platform spatial-UI guidelines, and by two independent open-source implementations across two engines, while every product keeps its own menus, content, skin, prefabs, pose thresholds, and placement values outside the shared Core.
non_claims: Admission does not claim legibility, comfort, reach, hand-tracking behaviour, eye-tracking behaviour, pointer precision, latency, panel visibility on a headset, or any named-device behaviour; those require a Device Lab receipt.
Admission does not transfer any Inventory presentation, renderer, XR composition, or device evidence to this family, and no UGUI adapter evidence transfers to the UI Toolkit adapter or the reverse.
